Duration::milliseconds¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::milliseconds() const

The Millisecond Field¶

milliseconds() extracts the three decimal digits immediately below the whole second. Its valid range is 0..999. Finer precision remains available through microseconds() and nanoseconds(); the fields are separate, so a fractional part of 0.005006007 seconds decomposes to 5 milliseconds, 6 microseconds, and 7 nanoseconds.

The method does not report total elapsed milliseconds. For example, a span of one second plus five milliseconds has component 5, while total().milliseconds() returns 1005. Negative values use the canonical nonnegative remainder, making -1 ns produce millisecond field 999.

Result Contract¶

The output is a newly allocated, shape-preserving Int64 Series. NaT lanes remain the exact Duration::kNaT sentinel. Extraction is O(numel), requires no floating-point conversion, and therefore preserves all nanosecond identity.

Examples¶

Example 1. Isolate the millisecond digits from a full-precision scalar.

std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::nanos(93'784'005'006'007LL).milliseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=5

Example 2. Observe normalization at negative boundaries.

constexpr std::int64_t hour = 3'600'000'000'000LL;
constexpr std::int64_t day = 86'400'000'000'000LL;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::nanos({-1, -hour, -day}).milliseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[999, 0, 0]

Example 3. Matrix structure and absence survive extraction.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {93'784'005'006'007LL, pluss::Duration::kNaT, -1, 0}, {2,2});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(values.milliseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡   5 -9223372036854775808 ⎤
⎣ 999                    0 ⎦

Example 4. No lanes are invented for an empty shape.

std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::zeros({2,0,3}).milliseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,0,3], strides=[0,3,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=0, contiguous=true)
[]

See Also¶

  • microseconds(): the next three fractional digits.

  • nanoseconds(): the final three fractional digits.

  • total().milliseconds(): complete elapsed milliseconds.
